title: PM Modi Inaugurates Bhogapuram Airport, Andhra Pradesh's First Greenfield Hub
excerpt: The Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport near Visakhapatnam opens with a 6-million passenger capacity and plans to transform North Coastal Andhra's economic landscape.
body:
• PM Modi inaugurated the Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport at Bhogapuram on August 1 — Andhra Pradesh's first greenfield airport
  • Built by GMR at a cost of Rs 4,000 crore, the airport has an initial capacity of 6 million passengers per year, scalable to over 40 million
  • The 3,800-metre runway can handle both domestic and international flights, with commercial operations set to begin immediately
  • Seven approach roads are being fast-tracked to connect the airport with Visakhapatnam, located 50 km away

Prime Minister Narendra Modi formally inaugurated the Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport at Bhogapuram on Friday, dedicating Andhra Pradesh's newest and third international airport to the nation. The greenfield facility near Visakhapatnam is the first of its kind in the state, built at a cost of approximately Rs 4,000 crore by GMR Visakhapatnam International Airport Limited, a subsidiary of GMR Airports Limited.

Built for Scale

The airport has been designed with an initial capacity of 6 million passengers per annum, scalable to more than 40 million in future phases. Its infrastructure includes a 3,800-metre Code 4E runway, a modern integrated passenger terminal, dedicated cargo facilities, and advanced airside systems capable of handling both domestic and international operations.

All eight major statutory and regulatory clearances required for commercial operations have been secured, including the Aerodrome Licence from the DGCA, security vetting from the Bureau of Civil Aviation Security, notification as an Immigration Check Post, and Customs notification under Section 8 of the Customs Act. Commercial flight operations are expected to begin within days of the inauguration.

In January, an Air India flight from Delhi landed successfully at Bhogapuram as part of a validation trial run, confirming the airport's operational readiness.

Gateway to North Coastal Andhra

Located about 50 km from Visakhapatnam city, the airport will serve as the primary aviation gateway for Visakhapatnam, Vizianagaram, Srikakulam, and neighbouring districts of southern Odisha and Chhattisgarh. The distance from the city centre has prompted accelerated road construction, with seven key approach roads and enhanced public transport services being developed to ensure seamless access.

"Bhogapuram International Airport will play a pivotal role in the development of North Andhra. It will create new opportunities and significantly improve the lives of ordinary people."

— N. Chandrababu Naidu, Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh

Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu, who conducted a high-level review meeting on inauguration arrangements, described the airport as a landmark for the region. The project was initiated during the TDP government in 2014 and accelerated by the present coalition government, with completion achieved within two years of the latest push.

Economic Catalyst

Beyond passenger connectivity, the airport is positioned as a driver of long-term economic development across North Coastal Andhra. Its dedicated cargo infrastructure and proximity to industrial corridors are expected to support export competitiveness in sectors including pharmaceuticals, electronics, seafood, information technology, and advanced manufacturing.

The Visakhapatnam Economic Region stands to benefit from improved logistics efficiency and trade connectivity. The state government's VMRDA 2041 vision plan, recently approved, envisions an integrated aerocity development around the airport to catalyse investment and urban growth.

The facility has also been developed with sustainability measures, incorporating renewable energy systems, rainwater harvesting, and energy-efficient infrastructure.

A First PM Visit in 43 Years

Modi's visit to inaugurate the airport carries symbolic weight for the region. According to reports, this marks the first visit by a sitting Prime Minister to the Vizianagaram district in 43 years, underscoring the political significance of the occasion for the ruling coalition.

Diaspora Connectivity

For the Telugu diaspora — particularly those with roots in Visakhapatnam, Vizianagaram, and Srikakulam — the international airport offers the prospect of direct connectivity to their home region. The existing Visakhapatnam airport's capacity constraints had long frustrated travellers, and the new facility is expected to attract airlines willing to operate routes previously considered unviable.
